desc: Establish order preservation: pieces never cross; sorted P maps monotonically to sorted targets; pieces can stack so m ≥ t required (not equal counts).
Recognize sample 2 impossibility is due to m < t (1 piece, 3 targets).
Derive feasibility condition for fixed k: monotone surjective assignment with |d_j| ≤ k, checked via greedy matching + gap-respecting absorption; hand-verified samples 1 and 3 (answers 3 and 5).
Decide algorithm: binary search + O(N) greedy check, O(ΣN log N) total — acceptable for ΣN ≤ 10⁶.

Stress-test against brute-force BFS for small N — found counterexample N=4, A='0110', B='1001' where matching succeeds at k=1 but BFS requires k=2 (right-mover positioned right of left-mover: pivot separability violated).
Fix absorption pass to respect monotone assignment gaps (unmatched piece between g_s and g_{s+1} must use Q_s or Q_{s+1}) — implemented, but shown insufficient alone.

Implement displacement sign-separation condition (no d<0 piece before a d>0 piece in piece order, with greedy target choice for absorbed pieces) and hand-verify on the N=4 counterexample plus all three samples.
Re-run BFS stress test for N ≤ 8 to confirm the augmented check matches brute force exactly.
Final review: edge cases (single piece, already-satisfied configuration k=0, forced stacking, pieces at boundaries) and confirm sample outputs 3, -1, 5.
